samples.question: What is the main contribution of the YOLO object detection framework?
samples.ground_truth: YOLO reframes object detection as a single regression problem, predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one forward pass, enabling real-time detection speeds.

samples.question: How does the self-attention mechanism work in Vision Transformers (ViT)?
samples.ground_truth: Vision Transformers split an image into fixed-size non-overlapping patches, embed each patch as a token, then apply multi-head self-attention so every token can attend to every other token, capturing global spatial context.

samples.question: What are the main trade-offs between speed and accuracy in object detection models?
samples.ground_truth: Faster models use lightweight backbones and single-stage detection heads but miss small or occluded objects. Accurate models use larger two-stage pipelines with feature pyramids at the cost of higher latency.

samples.question: How do multi-object tracking algorithms handle occlusion?
samples.ground_truth: Tracking algorithms combine appearance re-identification embeddings with Kalman filter motion prediction to estimate hidden positions, and use track management grace periods before deleting lost tracks.

samples.question: What is a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and what problem does it solve?
samples.ground_truth: FPN builds a top-down pathway with lateral connections that merges high-resolution low-level features with semantically rich high-level features, solving multi-scale detection by producing strong representations at every scale.

samples.question: What roles do the classification and regression heads play in anchor-based object detectors?
samples.ground_truth: The classification head predicts object category probabilities per anchor while the regression head predicts coordinate offsets to refine the anchor position and size to better fit the target bounding box.

samples.question: How does non-maximum suppression (NMS) work in object detection?
samples.ground_truth: NMS iteratively selects the highest-scoring box, suppresses all remaining boxes whose IoU with it exceeds a threshold, and repeats until no boxes remain, eliminating duplicate detections of the same object.

samples.question: What is the difference between one-stage and two-stage object detectors?
samples.ground_truth: Two-stage detectors first generate region proposals with an RPN then classify and refine them; one-stage detectors skip the proposal step and predict boxes and classes directly from feature maps in a single forward pass.

samples.question: How is IoU (Intersection over Union) used to evaluate object detection performance?
samples.ground_truth: IoU measures the overlap between predicted and ground-truth boxes as the area of intersection divided by the area of union. A detection is counted as correct when its IoU with the matching ground-truth box exceeds a threshold (commonly 0.5).

samples.question: What is the role of data augmentation in training object detection models?
samples.ground_truth: Data augmentation — including random cropping, flipping, colour jitter, and mosaic mixing — artificially expands training variety, improving robustness to scale, orientation, and lighting changes and reducing overfitting.
